explanation:
[EFFECT] Higher wind speed consistently reduces the model's predicted bike demand — the effect is predominantly negative and broadly monotonic. At very low wind speeds (roughly 0–7 km/h normalised ≈ 0–0.1), contributions are near zero or marginally positive, meaning wind has almost no impact at calm conditions. As wind speed rises beyond roughly 20 km/h (normalised ≈ 0.3), contributions turn noticeably negative, and above ~33 km/h (normalised ≈ 0.5) they become strongly negative, reaching as low as –0.7 in log space — equivalent to a substantial multiplicative drop in predicted rentals. The strongest suppression occurs at the highest wind speeds observed in the data.

[IMPORTANCE] Windspeed is ranked **8th out of 9 features** with a global importance of 0.020, making it one of the least influential predictors in the model. It contributes far less than top drivers such as the hour of day (0.833), year (0.200), or temperature (0.197), and only marginally more than the holiday flag (0.012).

[RECOMMENDATION] Because high wind noticeably suppresses predicted demand, on days forecast to be very windy (above roughly 20–33 km/h) the team can plan for moderately lower ridership and may reduce the number of bikes deployed or staff on duty at exposed stations — while keeping in mind that wind is a minor factor compared to the time of day or temperature.
